name: Fergie
notes: Solo pop out of the crossover-rap camp: 100–128 straight, backbeat on 2&4, with the signature ballad at 113 under an acoustic-folk surface. The harmonic fact is unusually specific and it is the model's spine — a documented **G–Csus2–D5** cell, I–IVsus2–V, "suspended and 5-voiced chords instead of full triads, which is why the ballads read as folk rather than pop". That is `susSubstitutionProb` at 0.46, the highest number of its kind in this section, over a I–IV–V family. Drums are stated as "simple drums" programmed by the producer rather than a kit player: "kick on 1 and 3, snare/clap on 2&4, 8th tambourine", with the electro tracks moving to four-on-the-floor with stacked claps — so the base is pinned to 8ths at a low fill density, the tambourine leads the percs and the clap offset tightens. The bass is programmed too — "long notes on the ballads, 8th-note synth bass on the uptempos" — hence `boom_chick` with a high root probability. The lead is documented as G3–C5 with a "verse conversational, chorus a repeated 2-bar cell", and the ~30-piece string section is the counter running as a sustained pad. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are all drum probabilities and the counter ratio; "simple" is a direction and 0.3 fill density is this author's reading of it. ⚠ **`bassline.rhythm` is `boom_chick`, not `reese_sustain`** — the research names the figure outright: *“programmed bass on roots (the producer handled bass and drum programming); long notes on the ballads, 8th-note synth bass on the uptempos”*. A held `reese_sustain` writes one note per chord and says the opposite of what the entry describes.
